architecture.mechanism: Sorption-based vapor capture — desiccants with high affinity for water spontaneously absorb water vapor from air, and airborne contaminants co-condense with water vapor, so a sorbent can both capture and reveal the presence of an escaping vapor.
architecture.intervention: Place labeled silica-gel/zeolite desiccant packs at the driver-side HVAC fresh-air intake and around suspect coolant points (radiator cap, heater core seams, hose clamps, overflow tank), then drive to operating temperature; inspect packs for coolant residue/weight gain and check the AC evaporator condensate drain for coolant contamination to pinpoint the source.
architecture.expected_effect: The sorbent absorbs the escaping coolant vapor before it reaches the cabin (eliminating the odor) and the residue pattern localizes the actual seep so it can be repaired rather than dismissed as normal.
architecture.falsification_test: After a full warm-up drive cycle, compare sorbent packs and a control pack placed away from the engine — if only the intake/heater-core packs show coolant residue or weight gain and cabin odor disappears while they are in place, vapor ingress is confirmed; if no pack picks up residue and the odor persists, the sorption hypothesis is falsified and a cooling-system pressure/leak test is required.
